sections.h2: How do sellers move a house quickly in Troy, Michigan?
sections.html:
A Troy owner can sell fast by pricing a listing to attract several offers, by selling privately to a known buyer, or by accepting an as-is cash purchase. Troy has a higher Census median home value than Sterling Heights, Taylor or Walker, so a few weeks of preparation can pay for itself, while a cash sale suits owners who cannot wait.

The Census Bureau puts the typical owner-occupied home at $420,300, and median household income at $120,045. At those values a buyer's inspection report carries weight. Sellers with a house that needs major work, an estate to settle, or a job relocation often skip that process and take a single offer from a buyer who will handle repairs.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good shape and you can allow time for inspections and a buyer's financing.
  • Sell privately only if you are comfortable preparing a purchase agreement and a deed that the Oakland County Register of Deeds will accept.
  • Take a cash offer when speed, privacy or the condition of the house matter more than the top price.

sections.h2: What is Troy, Michigan, and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Troy is an Oakland County city of about 33.5 square miles of land, with 88,733 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. Sterling Heights lies along its eastern border, and the city sits in the Detroit metropolitan area.

The earliest recorded land purchases came in 1819, and a settlement called Troy Corners formed after Johnson Niles bought 160 acres in the area that is now north-central Troy. Troy Township was organized in 1827. Pieces of the township later became Birmingham, Clawson and Royal Oak, and the remainder incorporated as the city of Troy in 1955, partly to stop neighboring cities from taking more land. The population jumped from 19,402 in 1960 to 39,419 in 1970 as Detroiters moved to the suburbs, and the 2020 Census counted 87,294.

Weather is a normal Great Lakes mix. Wikipedia's climate table for the 48098 ZIP code lists a January average low of 22 degrees Fahrenheit and about 32 inches of precipitation a year, so roof and gutter condition tend to come up in inspections.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Troy?
sections.html:
Troy stands apart on income, education and home value. Nearly two-thirds of adults 25 and older hold at least a bachelor's degree, and almost one in three residents was born abroad.

sections.h2: Which employers, malls and schools shape Troy demand?
sections.html:
Troy's business district along Big Beaver Road is the city's economic center, with automotive and financial offices, the Somerset Collection mall and its skywalk, the Oakland Mall and the Top of Troy tower. Walsh College and several university branch campuses are in the city, and the Troy Historic Village preserves ten structures that tell the city's early history.

Seven school districts serve Troy, and Troy School District covers most of the city, with twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, and two zoned high schools, Troy High and Athens High. Avondale, Birmingham and Warren Consolidated each run at least one elementary school inside the city. Bloomfield Hills and Royal Oak take in smaller pieces, and a small commercial area falls in Lamphere. The eastern campus of the International Academy is also in the Troy district.

Because of that patchwork, the district for a given house can differ from the neighbor's. Put the district name in the listing and the purchase paperwork, and ask the city assessor which district applies if you are unsure.

sections.h2: How do Troy assessments and tax bills work for a seller?
sections.html:
Troy's assessor sets values at 50% of market value, as the Michigan Constitution requires, and the office also handles the Principal Residence Exemption and the Property Transfer Affidavit programs. The assessing page projects that the city's combined State Equalized Value will exceed $10 billion for 2026.

  • Summer bills are mailed July 1 and payable through September 1 without penalty. A 4% penalty is added on the first business day after, and a half percent monthly interest starts October 1.
  • Winter bills are mailed December 1 and payable through February 14, with a 3% penalty after that date.
  • On March 1, unpaid current-year taxes go to the Oakland County Treasurer in Pontiac, at 248.858.0611, option 7.

The city bills for seven school districts, Oakland County, the Huron-Clinton Metropolitan Authority, the county art, zoo and transit authorities, Oakland Schools and the Macomb Intermediate School District. Because school millage differs by district, and because owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied rates differ, two Troy houses with the same value can get different bills. Homeowners who are 62 or older, disabled or eligible veterans with household income of $40,000 or less can apply to defer payment to April 30, with the application due by September 15.

After your sale, the buyer's taxable value resets, because Michigan uncaps taxable value in the calendar year after a transfer of ownership. Tell your buyer to expect a different bill, and ask the Treasurer's Office at 248.524.3333 how prorations are handled for your closing date.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and recording steps apply in Oakland County?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state and county transfer taxes, payable to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed (MCL 207.523). The state tax is $3.75 per $500 of value (MCL 207.525). For a county with fewer than 2,000,000 people, the county tax in MCL 207.504 is 55 cents per $500, and a county with 2,000,000 or more may set up to 75 cents. Ask the Oakland County Register of Deeds to confirm the county amount before closing.

The Register of Deeds takes questions at 248-858-0597 or deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office records deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records, and its Super Index lets you view documents recorded since January 1, 1964.

The exemptions in MCL 207.526 include deeds from a parent to a child or grandchild, transfers in foreclosure, and conveyances without a stated price ordered by a court. The deed has to cite the exemption on its face, and a missing citation means the tax is collected.

sections.h2: Which Troy codes should you handle before showing a house?
sections.html:
The city's code enforcement office lists several rules that tend to produce notices around a sale. They are worth a walk around the property before photos or an open house.

  • Lawn grass and weeds may not exceed 8 inches from May 1 to October 31, and the owner maintains the strip between sidewalk and road.
  • Owners must clear snow deeper than 2 inches and any ice from the public sidewalk within 24 hours after the storm ends.
  • Cars stored outside on private property must be licensed and operable, and recreational vehicles cannot sit on the street or vacant lots.
  • Temporary signs are allowed on private property with limits, and signs in the public right-of-way are removed by the city.
  • Trash goes to the curb no sooner than 5 p.m. the day before, and branches must be trimmed to 8 feet above the sidewalk.

Keep an open house or yard sign on your own lot, which avoids the city removing it. Clearing these items before a showing keeps a complaint from landing during your listing.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Troy home worth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median value of $420,300 for owner-occupied homes in Troy for 2020 to 2024. Your own house can fall well above or below that figure depending on age, condition, lot and school district.

faqs.q: When are Troy property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer bills are payable through September 1 and winter bills through February 14 without penalty. Unpaid taxes move to the Oakland County Treasurer on March 1, with more fees and interest.

faqs.q: Does a Troy sale reset property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, for the buyer. Under Michigan law a transfer of ownership uncaps taxable value in the following calendar year, so the new owner's bill can exceed yours.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Troy house in?
faqs.a: Troy School District covers most of the city, but Avondale, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Lamphere, Royal Oak and Warren Consolidated also reach into Troy. Check the address with the city assessor or the district.

faqs.q: Where does a Troy deed get recorded?
faqs.a: Deeds for Troy properties are recorded with the Oakland County Register of Deeds, reachable at 248-858-0597. The transfer tax is paid to the county treasurer unless the deed cites an exemption.
